title: Green, Social, Sustainability and Sustainability-Linked Bonds in Developing Countries: How Can Donors Support Public Sector Issuances?
summary: This OECD report analyzes the potential for scaling green, social, sustainability, and sustainability-linked (GSSS) bond issuances by public sector actors in developing countries, and provides recommendations for donor support. The paper notes that GSSS bond activity remains concentrated in developed markets, with considerable untapped potential in low and middle-income countries.
key_points: GSSS bond activity is concentrated in developed markets; developing countries represent untapped potential
The report was mandated by the G20 Development Working Group under Italy's 2021 Presidency
ODA-eligible emerging market issuers are more likely to use sustainability and sustainability-linked bonds compared to developed market issuers
Sustainability-linked bond (SLB) issuances have rapidly increased, including in developing countries
SLB targets mainly relate to climate objectives, with coupon rate increases triggered by failure to meet targets
Donors can support through four 'i's: infrastructure, issuances, insurance, and investment
Key challenges include lack of bankable projects, weak financial markets, debt sustainability concerns, complex public budgeting, and limited localization of international standards
why_it_matters: This research paper examines how donors can support public sector GSSS bond issuances in developing countries. While it provides useful background on ESG bond market trends and development finance mechanisms, it is a policy recommendation document rather than a source of market-moving information or market structure dynamics.
